summary: babel-plugin-linaria-css-to-undefined ships preinstall dropper that runs an obfuscated Bun payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/..., chmods it executable, and invokes it against the shipped math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) obfuscated with a string-array rotator (function WV8StW performing shift/push over a ~1000-entry lookup table) — opaque to Node-based supply-chain scanners. setup.mjs itself uses _0xXXXX identifier obfuscation. The manifest advertises the package as a small Babel plugin (lib/index.js is ~85 readable lines authored under the ornikar/Christophe Hurpeau identity), but the legitimate upstream has no preinstall hook and ships no Bun binary. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern — a Node lifecycle hook fetching a second language runtime purely to execute a large obfuscated payload unrelated to the package's stated purpose — combined with impersonation of a known Babel plugin, is a trojanized package: `npm install` on any project that pulls this dependency executes the obfuscated Bun payload on the build host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
